description: We Are Team VORTEX and This is our Team
summary:
Chronicles of Silence is an interactive 3D space archaeology atlas and STEM storytelling web application built for school-age learners (ages 10–18) and educators. While active missions capture global headlines, dozens of retired pioneers—including the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, Surveyor 3, Lunokhod 1, Opportunity, InSight, and Ingenuity—rest silently across the Moon and Mars.

Our platform transforms dense archival telemetry into an accessible, living museum. Using a dual-planet WebGL interface grounded in NASA Solar System Treks, LROC, and HiRISE data, students explore real landing sites, toggle between empathetic first-person machine memoirs and forensic engineering telemetry, and hear stories narrated aloud via Web Speech synthesis. Users can also scrub a time-lapse degradation slider to simulate thermal shock and dust accumulation, sonify Opportunity’s final power loss, and test safe Artemis landing distances using our NASA SP-2011-3422 rocket plume calculator.

Chronicles of Silence reframes discarded hardware from "space debris" into humanity's first extraterrestrial cultural heritage sites and vital material-science benchmarks for future deep-space exploration.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? CHRONICLES OF SILENCE: The Extraterrestrial Archaeological Register & Field Guide is a client-side interactive web application designed to document, visualize, and tell the stories of NASA’s discarded equipment and relics left behind on the Moon and Mars. Users can navigate through a structured archival grid and sidebar interface to inspect specific lunar and Martian artifacts. The platform features a real-time interactive canvas that simulates environmental degradation—such as thermal cycling on the Moon and aeolian (wind-driven) erosion on Mars—allowing users to see how extreme extraterrestrial conditions affect hardware over decades. Additionally, it integrates synthesized ambient space audio and narrated field logs to create an immersive storytelling experience.

What benefits does it have & what is the intended impact?

  • Preserving Space Heritage: Instead of viewing decommissioned rovers, landers, and instruments merely as "space debris," the platform reframes them as vital milestones in human space exploration.
  • Accessible STEM Storytelling: By combining historical mission data with interactive physics-based visualizers, it transforms static NASA archives into an engaging, educational experience for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts worldwide.
  • Zero-Barrier Access: Built purely as a lightweight client-side application, it runs smoothly directly in standard web browsers without requiring heavy downloads or specialized

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Core Web Tech: HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS), and vanilla JavaScript.
  • Graphics, Audio & Accessibility: Three.js / WebGL and HTML5 Canvas for 3D rendering and thermal/aeolian decay vector simulations; Web Audio API for procedural ambient sound synthesis; and the Web Speech API for automated voice narration of the field logs.
  • Development Environment: Developed and tested on Ubuntu Linux and Windows using VS Code, Git, and GitHub.

How is your project creative? We approached space history through the lens of extraterrestrial archaeology. Rather than presenting a standard text-heavy encyclopedia, we designed the interface as an authentic aerospace field register—complete with a deep-space telemetry color palette, dynamic decay vector visualizations, and procedural audio cues that evoke the isolation and permanence of hardware resting on alien worlds.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific & Environmental Realism: Our team carefully differentiated between the degradation mechanisms of the Moon (vacuum, micrometeorite bombardment, extreme thermal shifts) and Mars (thin CO₂ atmosphere, dust storms, wind erosion) so the visual simulations reflect actual planetary science.
  • User Experience & Performance: We prioritized fast load times, clear visual hierarchy, and intuitive navigation so users can seamlessly switch between historical storytelling and technical telemetry data.
